items.title: Brazil's tax authority open-sources its tax calculator on GitHub under MIT
items.summary: Brazil's tax authority has released its tax calculator as open-source software on GitHub, promoting transparency in tax reform. This initiative allows developers to contribute to and improve the tool, fostering collaboration and innovation in public sector software.

items.title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
items.summary: Recent research demonstrates that language models can autonomously adjust their own weights, potentially leading to more efficient training processes. This capability could revolutionize how developers approach model optimization and deployment.

items.title: Valkey kills the skiplist, cuts sorted set overhead by up to 43%
items.summary: The Valkey project has replaced the traditional skiplist with a B+ tree structure, achieving significant reductions in overhead for sorted sets. This advancement can lead to improved performance in data-intensive applications, making it a noteworthy development for engineers focused on system efficiency.

items.title: ClawDOS – An AI coding agent for DOS
items.summary: ClawDOS is an innovative AI coding agent designed to assist in programming for DOS environments. This tool could enhance productivity for developers working with legacy systems, bridging the gap between modern AI capabilities and older technologies.

items.title: FBI reportedly investigating apparent hack of its criminal database
items.summary: The FBI is currently investigating a potential breach of its criminal database, raising concerns about data security and integrity. This incident highlights the importance of robust security measures in protecting sensitive information within government systems.
